decisions.reason: As a close-to-core 2023 launch that stayed on the home page and was presented as a flagship, it carries high sunk costs and public commitment, so management is very likely to persist with it.

This software extends the firm's established QA and workflow capabilities and has been maintained with its own page since launch, so disappointing early results would likely be treated as temporary rather than grounds for withdrawal.
The CT phantom fits the firm's established medical imaging QA offer, and as a recent 2024 launch management would usually give it more time rather than quickly admit a mistaken introduction.

Because this mammography phantom is more distant from the core offer and lacks strong visible strategic emphasis, it is more vulnerable, but its recent launch still makes escalation and patience more likely than an immediate exit.

This full field mammography phantom is also distant from the firm's main trajectory and not publicly highlighted as central, yet the firm has already listed it and would likely continue at least another year before conceding failure.

A flagship 2024 product line with several models that builds on the firm's established imaging QA capabilities represents substantial investment and visible commitment, which strongly favors retention.
